photos.author: Nithajay
photos.description: Lauki Kofta curry is very popular curry recipe from Hyderabad. Koftas are deep fried balls of any ingredient which are then cooked in a thick onion-tomato gravy. In this dish, the koftas are made of lauki or bottle gourd. Lauki or bottle gourd is also known as ghiya or doodhi or dudhi or Opo squash. In this summer season, it is available in all Indian veggie market. It has more water content, so it is helpful to deal with the heat, and it prevents exhaustion in hot Indian summer.

photos.description: The image is the photograph of a bowl of Chahao Kheer, a very popular dessert of Manipur. Chahao is an aromatic rice, dark purple (almost black) in colour, grown in Manipur. The kheer (payasam) is prepared using the Chahao rice, milk, coconut and raisins. The above photograph was taken at the guest house canteen of Manipur University.
photos.review_note: One steel bowl of chahao kheer - purple rice pudding with milk - on a tablecloth, with a spoon.

photos.title: File:A traditional Bengali dish served on a banana leaf surrounded by flower petals.jpg
photos.author: Antik Jana
photos.description: This photo shows a typical traditional Bengali thali consists of various ethnic food items like fice , fish curry , served on a banana leaf for the bride in the ritual event of 'Aiburobhaat' which is a ceremonial eating event before the marriage of an individual , where both the bride and the groom have to visit the houses of their relatives . The relatives then offer a wide variety of dishes to the bride/ groom.The dishes consist of 'Papad','Misti doi' or sweet curd , the traditional ethnic Bengali rosogolla,Sandesh , Tomato Chutney, Chicken Curry , Fish Curry , Daal , A fish fry ,'Shaakh Bhaja', 'Begun bhaja' or Eggplant fry , Potato fry or ' Aloo Bhaja' and also containing few cucumber and onion pieces
photos.reject_reason: a styled flat-lay - marigold petals scattered on a printed cloth - with eight items of which three I could not name (a yellow shoru, a white dessert, a second dark curry). Exactly the khichdi rejection again: a truth I cannot defend is not added

photos.reject_reason: Filed on Commons as 'boryani', and it is a steel bowl of yellow rice beside a thick brown gravy. I cannot call that biryani honestly: the grain is short and uniformly yellow rather than long-grain and layered, and there is no visible meat. The only other reading is rice with dal - and dal is one of the four classes this batch exists to avoid growing. So the two available labels are one guess and one regression, and a photo that can only be labelled by guessing is not added

photos.title: File:Fried Fish, Lamb Curry, French Beans with Basmatic Rice - Tastes of Singapore (2144887899).jpg
photos.author: Alpha from Melbourne, Australia
photos.description: Fried Fish, Lamb Curry, French Beans with Basmatic Rice - Tastes of Singapore 2 meat and 1 veg rice special AUD6.50 Good lamb curry and crispy fried fish. I love the turmeric and other spices used to marinate fried fish! --- Feeling the need for some Malaysian spice. Not Indian, not Korean, not Japanese. So we decided to give Tastes of Singapore a go. We had heard that they do a decent satay. The food is definitely very typical of a Mamak stall in Singapore or Malaysia. We didn't have any (lamb or chicken) satays this time, but they looked and smelled quite good, and were done on the grill! They even have tables outside, and when it is 36°C in the shade, really makes it feel like a Mamak stall in Malaysia! Best of all, the food is very reasonably priced! Taste Of Singapore 162 Clayton Rd Clayton 3168 (03) 9544 7865 Photos: - Fried Fish, Lamb Curry, French Beans with Basmati Rice - Mee Rebus - Teh Tarik 20080102: A second visit! - Lamb Murtabak AUD6 - Mee Siam AUD6.50 - Decor
photos.reject_reason: four non-staple components on one plate - sauteed french beans, white rice, a bone-in lamb curry and a piece of fried fish - plus a diner in frame. class_of() takes the first non-staple, so the class would be decided by the order I happened to write the truth in, which is me choosing the class rather than the photograph

photos.title: File:South Indian Celebration.jpg
photos.author: Varundn
photos.description: The image shows a typical South Indian meal served to every guest during celebrations( this picture was taken during a naming ceremony) on a green banana leaf. It contains varieties of food. The interesting thing about serving is that, everyone is served with specific food on a particular part of the banana leaf. The Kheer( sweet) is on the right bottom, the flavoured rice with papad is on the left bottom and plain rice in the middle with a small amount of dal(yellowish) on top of it with ghee. And, the top portion of the leaf is filled with lighter items. ( L-R) Salt, Mango Pickle, a mixture of sweet corn with coconut shavings, a mixture of soaked dal with coconut shavings and carrot, a thick curry( mildly sweet usually) and two vegetable curries.
photos.reject_reason: a sadya spread on a banana leaf: rice, a papad, salt, and three red and orange preparations I cannot each name. The dominant component is rice, which is a STAPLE, so class_of() would fall through the staple rule to the fallback and score the case as whatever came first - a class from the fallback rather than from a judgement
